title: Batching & KV-Cache Sensitivity Evaluation for Latency vs Quality
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Quantify the latency vs. quality tradeoffs introduced by changes to batching and KV-cache configuration across representative workloads. This ticket scopes a set of controlled evals, production replays, and canary checks that measure (1) latency percentiles and throughput, (2) model-quality regressions on curated prompt sets, and (3) statistical correlation between batching/windowing and cache hit patterns. We will produce actionable guidance for default profiles and an automated alert threshold tied to the quality-monitoring pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Run matrix of experiments covering target batch sizes and batching windows for 3 model families and collect p50/p95 latency and token throughput
Measure quality drop (<2% relative for core QA and completion tasks) across base eval-suite and customer-derived prompt sets
Produce a recommendations doc with conservative default configurations and a dynamic policy for burst traffic
Create dashboard tabs and regression alerts in Optimize evals pipeline linked to PRs and rollout policies
plan_steps: 1) Build experiment harness: extend eval-runner to vary batching_window_ms, max_batch_size, cache_ttl, and cache_warmup behavior
2) Select workloads: interactive chat (low-latency), bulk document summarization (throughput), and retrieval-augmented generation prompts
3) Prepare datasets: combine internal eval-suite with anonymized production replay slice and 5 customer prompt packs
4) Execute controlled experiments on dedicated small cluster to avoid noisy neighbors
5) Analyze quality: use pairwise A/B comparisons, significance tests (bootstrap), and per-prompt fail-regression tracking
6) Run limited production canary with automated rollback if quality delta > threshold
7) Publish guidance and hook into console recommendations and Optimize suggestions
metrics: mean_prompt_quality_score (composite from NLI overlap + BLEU-like score)
